reasoning_traces.think:
The three core primitives form a triadic risk model: leakage in free-tier undermines conversion, perceptual sameness erodes willingness to pay, and shallow elite offerings trigger churn. These risks operate in a feedback loop where each failure mode degrades the others—leakage lowers perceived value, which increases churn, weakening the business case for premium tiers. The system's resilience hinges on maintaining distinct value layers and validating each tier’s utility against user expectations. Each primitive maps to a specific regime of trust and value delivery, forming a dualistic structure: one side governs access control (free vs paid), the other governs perceived benefit (tier differentiation). This duality manifests as a risk landscape where trust and conversion are co-dependent variables. The failure modes reflect systemic vulnerabilities in pricing architecture, where misalignment between perceived and actual value leads to cascading losses in customer lifetime value and revenue stability.
